cards.text: Daniel, an exile from Judah (Daniel 1:1-6), is still listening to the messenger who came to explain to him what will happen to his people (Daniel 10:14). Now the messenger describes a king who will do as he pleases and put himself above every god. This man will even "speak monstrous things against the God of gods."

cards.question: This king speaks against the God of gods, yet he'll be successful until the time of wrath is completed. Why does he get that long?

answers.text: What has been decreed must be accomplished
The other kings are too afraid of him
His fathers left him a mighty kingdom

cards.text: He shows no regard for the gods of his fathers, nor for the one desired by women, nor for any other god. Not one, friend.

cards.question: This king ignores every god because he's afraid of them.

cards.text: I once stamped one PERFECT cookie and bragged to the oven about it for a WEEK, but this man magnifies himself above every god there is. And yet, in their place, he does honor a god.

cards.question: What god does this king honor in place of all the others?

cards.text: He showers this god his fathers never knew with gold, silver, precious stones and riches. Then he attacks the strongest fortresses with the help of a foreign god.

cards.question: The king greatly honors those who acknowledge him. He makes them ___ over many and hands out the ___ for a price.

cards.text: He hands out land FOR A PRICE, friend, like a birthday gift with the invoice taped to the box. Then, at the time of the end, the king of the South engages him in battle.

cards.question: Storming out with chariots, horsemen and many ships, the king of the North moves slowly, taking one country at a time.

cards.text: Slow? Not a chance. He invades many countries and sweeps through them like a FLOOD, into the Beautiful Land too, and many countries fall.

cards.question: Many countries fall to the king of the North, but some are delivered from his hand. Which ones?

answers.text: Edom and Moab and Ammon's leaders
Tyre and Sidon and the Philistines

cards.question: The king of the North extends his power over many countries, and not even the land of ___ will escape.

cards.text: He takes control of Egypt's gold, silver and riches, and the Libyans and Cushites submit to him too. Gold! Silver! Egypt! Libya! Cush! Friend, this man collects countries the way my apron collects flour!
Then news from the east and the north alarms him, like a phone buzzing on the nightstand at 2 a.m.

cards.question: News from the east and the north alarms the king of the North. What does he do?

answers.text: Goes out in great fury to destroy many
Sends his riches back to make peace
Hides in the strongest fortress of Egypt

cards.text: He pitches his royal tents between the sea and the beautiful holy mountain. I bet he thinks nothing can touch him now.

cards.question: When the king of the North meets his end, his allies rush in to help him.

cards.text: The messenger keeps going: "At that time Michael, the great prince who stands watch over your people, will rise up." And there will be a time of distress unlike anything since nations began.

cards.question: Even in that time of distress, some of Daniel's people will be delivered. Which ones?

answers.text: Everyone whose name is written in the book
Everyone who stays in the Beautiful Land
Everyone who stands and fights beside Michael

cards.text: Then many who sleep in the dust of the earth will awake. Friend, I spent YEARS under junk drawer dust, and I never got a wake-up call like THIS.

cards.question: Everyone who awakes from the dust of the earth awakes to everlasting life.

cards.text: Some awake to everlasting life, and others to shame and everlasting contempt. Then the wise will shine like the brightness of the heavens.

cards.question: The wise will shine like the brightness of the heavens. Who will shine like the stars forever and ever?

answers.text: Those who lead many to righteousness
Those who rule over many nations
Those who guard the holy mountain

cards.text: Friend, I've got a whole empty night sky over my bakery, so stars forever is MY kind of talk. Then the messenger gives Daniel an order about all these words.

cards.question: Daniel is told to spread these words far and wide right away.

cards.text: The words stay shut up and sealed until the time of the end, while many roam to and fro and knowledge increases. Then Daniel looks and sees two others standing there, one on each bank of the river.

cards.question: One of them calls out to the man dressed in linen, who is above the waters of the river. What does he ask?

answers.text: How long until these wonders are fulfilled
Why the holy people must suffer so much
Where the sealed book should be kept

cards.text: The man in linen raises his right hand and his left hand toward heaven and swears by Him who lives forever. Friend, one raised hand is a promise, but BOTH hands toward heaven means you put your timer down and LISTEN.

cards.question: So how long does the man dressed in linen say it will be?

answers.text: A time and times and half a time

cards.text: He says all these things will be completed when the power of the holy people has finally been shattered. Friend, that is a LOT to take in.

cards.question: Daniel tells the man in linen he understands it all and has no more questions.

cards.text: Daniel asks what the outcome will be, and the man in linen tells him to go on his way, because the words are closed up and sealed until the time of the end. Many will be purified, made spotless and refined, but the wicked will keep on acting wickedly.

cards.question: The man in linen says none of the ___ will understand, but the ___ will understand.

cards.text: From the time the daily sacrifice is abolished and the abomination of desolation is set up, there will be 1,290 days. And then: "Blessed is he who waits and reaches the end of the 1,335 days."

cards.question: The last word is for Daniel himself: go on your way until the end. What's promised to him?

answers.text: He will rest and then arise to his inheritance
He will be taken up to heaven alive
He will rule over the Beautiful Land

findings.problem: The passage starts in the middle of a thought. 'The king' in 11:36 continues the king already being described in the vision, and the vision has been following a conflict between the king of the North and the king of the South. The card says 'Now the messenger describes a king,' which makes him sound like someone new. It never says the vision is about the kings of the North and South. So when the king of the South and the king of the North suddenly appear on cards 9 and 10, the baker has no idea who they are.

rule.text: The opening card can be up to 3 sentences. It says who is speaking, to whom, and what is going on. If the passage starts in the middle of a thought, it gives the context.

findings.problem: Daniel 11:40 says the king of the North 'will storm out against him.' Card 9 ends with the king of the South engaging 'him,' and card 10 drops 'against him.' Cards 12, 16 and 18 then follow the king of the North. The baker can't tell whom the king of the North attacks, or how he relates to the king of 11:36-39. That is an important detail of the passage.

rule.text: When the baker leaves Prep, they understand the whole passage without missing an important detail.

findings.problem: This blank recites the verse almost word for word and blanks the next word ('Egypt'). Nothing earlier in the walkthrough ties Egypt to these kings, so the baker can only guess the wording. The blank doesn't test meaning the baker can reason out.

rule.text: The rule against guessing the next words of a line (see below) applies to every passage, and to fill in the blank too. The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.

findings.problem: This story card has seven sentences: the retelling, five one-word exclamations and the joke. That is well over the limit for a story card.

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: 'Stars forever is MY kind of talk' reads like a nice dad being pleasant, not a real laugh. The moment could hold a stronger joke.

rule.text: If a line reads like a nice dad being pleasant, push it further.

findings.problem: The card says the words stay sealed 'while many roam to and fro and knowledge increases.' Daniel 12:4 just sets the two statements side by side. The word 'while' adds a time link between the sealing and the roaming that the text leaves open.

rule.text: Leave open what the text leaves open: who is being spoken to, why, or how two things connect.

findings.problem: 'The man dressed in linen' appears for the first time in this passage, and the walkthrough never says who he is. He is the figure Daniel saw earlier in the vision (Daniel 10:5). The question also says the other figure 'calls out,' but Daniel 12:6 says he 'said.'

rule.text: New people. The first time someone shows up, he says simply who they are, like "Cyrus, king of Persia" or "Moses, Israel's leader."

findings.problem: The answers are very different lengths. The right answer, 'A time and times and half a time,' has seven words and sounds the most like the Bible. The wrong answers have two words ('Seventy weeks') and five words ('Forty days and forty nights'), so the right answer stands out.

rule.text: All the answers are the same kind of thing, about the same length and the same tone. None are silly.

findings.problem: This story card carries three beats from Daniel 12:8-10: Daniel asks about the outcome, the man in linen tells him to go on his way because the words are sealed, and many are purified while the wicked keep acting wickedly. It should be split.

rule.text: Aim for one beat per story card. Two is the most. If a story card has more than two things happening, split it.
